insider_note: Two answers are expected here, not one: (c − 17/6)² = 121/36 gives c = 14/3 and c = 1, and c = 1 is the value most students drop because they take only the positive root.

steps.label: Solve for the centre
steps.margin_note: Third printed mark, tagged "1 Mark". Double (2) so the y coefficients match, then add.
steps.memory_tip: Double equation (2) to get 2x₁ + 2y₁ − 10 = 0, then add to (1).

lines.text: Double (2) so the y₁ terms cancel on adding:

steps.why: Equation (1) has −2y₁ and equation (2) doubled has +2y₁, so adding removes y₁ at once. The centre has sixths in it, which is expected once a 6 appears in the coefficient.
common_mistakes: Adding (1) and (2) without doubling (2), so y₁ does not cancel.
Writing 5 − 13/6 as 17/6 with the wrong sign, giving −17/6.

steps.memory_tip: A square equals a square, so take the plus and the minus root. Two values of c come out.

Take the square root of both sides:

steps.why: Substituting D(0, c) into the circle gives a square equal to a number, and a square has two square roots. Both give a genuine fourth point on the circle, so both values of c are answers.
common_mistakes: Taking only the positive root and reporting c = 14/3 alone.
Cancelling the 36 too early and losing the sixths.
